voices.note: the Gemara's own voice of this piska: its questions (מאי, מיבעי ליה, למה לי, אטו, ותו ליכא, מנלן), its unattributed answers and derashot on new lemmas, the narrative of 12b.7-8, 13a.22-23, 16a.4-11, 16a.14, 16a.17, its kashya/teyuvta at 14a.9 and 15a.4
R' Yehuda (bar Ilai) as cited in the baraitot of 12a.13, 13a.11, 13a.18, 14b.12, 15b.14
R' Elazar (ben Pedat): 12a.18, 13a.20, 13a.24-13b.6, and transmitter of R' Chanina at 15a.16-15b.6
Ahasuerus, whose words the narrators report
Haman, whose words Rava (13b.16-19) and the stam's narrative (16a.4-10) report
Mordechai, whose words the stam's narrative reports
Queen Esther, whose words R' Levi (15b.7-8) and the stam (16a.17) report
תניא (13a.10-12): R' Meir, R' Yehuda, R' Nechemya, Ben Azzai, R' Yehoshua ben Korcha on Hadassa/Esther
Jacob the patriarch, speaker in R' Elazar's account (13b.3)
Rachel, speaker in R' Elazar's account (13b.3-5)
Bigtan and Teresh, whose conversation R' Yochanan reports (13b.10-11)

props.gloss_en: the verse: 'and he raised Hadassa, that is Esther' (Esth 2:7) -- she is called both Hadassa and Esther
R' Meir: her name was Esther; she was called Hadassa after the righteous, who are called myrtles (hadassim)
and so it says: 'and he stood among the myrtles' (Zech 1:8)
R' Yehuda: her name was Hadassa; she was called Esther because she concealed (mesateret) her words
as it is said: 'Esther did not reveal her people' (Esth 2:20)
R' Nechemya: her name was Hadassa; she was called Esther because the nations called her after Istahar [the moon/Venus]
Ben Azzai: Esther was neither tall nor short but of medium height, like a myrtle
R' Yehoshua ben Korcha: Esther was greenish, and a thread of grace was drawn over her
the verse: 'for she had neither father nor mother... and when her father and mother died' (Esth 2:7) -- the second clause is the object of למה לי
Rav Acha: when [her mother] conceived her, her father died; when she bore her, her mother died
a tanna in R' Meir's name: do not read 'for a daughter' (levat) but 'for a house' (levayit) [i.e. a wife]

and so it says: 'the poor man had nothing but one little ewe lamb... it lay in his bosom and was to him as a daughter' (2 Sam 12:3) -- because it lay in his bosom was it to him a daughter? rather, a wife; so here too, a wife
'the seven maidens' (Esth 2:9): Rava -- she counted the days of the week by them
'and he advanced her and her maidens': Rav -- he fed her Jewish food
Shmuel: he fed her pigs' necks
R' Yochanan: legumes
and so it says: 'the steward took away their food and gave them legumes' (Dan 1:16)
what is 'oil of myrrh' (Esth 2:12)? R' Chiya bar Abba: stacte
Rav Huna: olive oil from olives not yet a third grown
a baraita, R' Yehuda: anpakinon is oil of olives not yet a third grown; one anoints with it because it removes hair and softens the skin
'in the evening she came and in the morning she returned' (Esth 2:14): R' Yochanan -- from that wicked one's disgrace we learned his praise: he did not have relations by day
'and Esther found favour' (Esth 2:15): R' Elazar -- this teaches that to each one she seemed to be of his own nation
'the tenth month, the month of Tevet' (Esth 2:16) -- a month when body benefits from body
'more than all the women... more than all the virgins' (Esth 2:17): Rav -- if he wished to taste a virgin's taste, he tasted it; a non-virgin's, he tasted it
'and the king made a great feast' (Esth 2:18): he made a feast and she did not reveal [her origin] to him; he lowered taxes and she did not reveal; he sent gifts and she did not reveal
[Mordechai's counsel, as the stam narrates:] a woman is jealous only of another woman's thigh
and even so she did not reveal to him, as written: 'Esther did not reveal her kindred' (Esth 2:20)
R' Elazar on 'He does not withdraw His eyes from the righteous' (Job 36:7): as reward for Rachel's modesty Saul descended from her, and as reward for Saul's modesty Esther descended from him
the verse: 'and Jacob told Rachel that he was her father's brother' (Gen 29:12) -- object of the difficulty: was he not her father's sister's son?
[R' Elazar:] 'her father's brother' means: I am his brother in trickery
Jacob: will you marry me? ... I am his brother in trickery
Rachel: yes, but my father is a trickster and you cannot prevail against him
Rachel: is it permitted for the righteous to act with trickery?
Jacob: yes -- 'with the pure You show Yourself pure, and with the crooked You show Yourself subtle' (2 Sam 22:27)
Rachel: I have a sister older than me and he will not marry me off before her; [Jacob] gave her signs
when night came she said: now my sister will be shamed -- and she gave them to her
the verse: 'and in the morning, behold, it was Leah' (Gen 29:25) -- object of מכלל דעד השתא לאו לאה היא
because of the signs Rachel gave Leah, he did not know until then; therefore she merited that Saul descended from her
and Saul's modesty? as written 'but of the matter of the kingdom he did not tell him' (1 Sam 10:16); he merited that Esther descended from him
and R' Elazar said: when the Holy One allots greatness to a man, He allots it to his sons and grandsons to the end of all generations, as said 'He sets them forever and they are exalted' (Job 36:7)
and if he grows arrogant, the Holy One lowers him, as said 'and if they are bound in fetters' (Job 36:8)
'and Esther did Mordechai's word' (Esth 2:20): R' Yirmeya -- she would show menstrual blood to the Sages
'as when she was raised with him': Rabba bar Lima -- she would rise from Ahasuerus's bosom, immerse, and sit in Mordechai's bosom
R' Chiya bar Abba in R' Yochanan's name: the Holy One angered a master at his servants to do a righteous man's will -- Joseph, as said 'and there was with us a Hebrew youth' (Gen 41:12)
[and] servants at their masters to do a miracle for a righteous man -- Mordechai, as written 'and the matter became known to Mordechai' (Esth 2:22)
R' Yochanan: Bigtan and Teresh were two Tarsians speaking Tarsian; they did not know that Mordechai sat in the Chamber of Hewn Stone and knew seventy languages
Bigtan and Teresh: since she came we have seen no sleep; come, let us put poison in the cup so that he dies
one to the other: are not my watch and yours different? -- I will keep my watch and yours
and this is what is written: 'the matter was investigated and found' (Esth 2:23) -- that they were not found at their posts
'after these things' (Esth 3:1) -- after what? Rava: after the Holy One created the cure for the blow
Resh Lakish: the Holy One strikes Israel only if He first creates their cure, as said 'when I would heal Israel, the iniquity of Ephraim is uncovered' (Hos 7:1)
but the nations are not so: He strikes them and afterwards creates their cure, as said 'the Lord will strike Egypt, striking and healing' (Isa 19:22)
'to lay hands on Mordechai alone' (Esth 3:6): Rava -- first Mordechai alone, then Mordechai's people, the Rabbis, and finally all the Jews
a tanna: when the lot fell on Adar he rejoiced greatly: the lot fell on the month Moses died -- not knowing that on the seventh of Adar he died and on the seventh of Adar he was born
Moses died on the seventh of Adar and was born on the seventh of Adar
'there is one people' (Esth 3:8): Rava -- there is none who knew slander like Haman
Haman: come, let us destroy them. Ahasuerus: I fear their God, lest He do to me as to my predecessors. Haman: 'yeshno' -- they have slept (yashnu) from the commandments
Ahasuerus: I fear their God, lest He do to me as He did to my predecessors
Ahasuerus: there are Rabbis among them. Haman: they are one people [they will be judged together]

Haman: lest you say I make a bald patch in your kingdom -- they are scattered among the peoples; lest you say there is profit from them -- 'dispersed' (meforad), like a mule (pereda) that bears no fruit; lest you say there is a province of them -- 'in all the provinces of your kingdom'

Haman: 'their laws differ' -- they do not eat of ours or marry with us; 'they do not keep the king's laws' -- they idle away the year with 'today is Shabbat, today is Passover'; 'it does not profit the king' -- they eat, drink and scorn the king; a fly in one's cup he tosses out and drinks, but if my lord the king touches his cup, he dashes it to the ground and does not drink
Resh Lakish: it was revealed before Him who spoke and the world came to be that Haman would weigh shekels against Israel; therefore He put their shekels before his
the mishna: on the first of Adar they announce the shekels and the mixed species
R' Abba: Ahasuerus and Haman are like two men, one with a mound in his field and one with a ditch in his field
the ditch-owner said: sell me your mound! he said: take it for free, and gladly! -- ['the silver is given to you, and the people', Esth 3:11]
R' Abba bar Kahana: the removal of the ring was greater than the forty-eight prophets and seven prophetesses -- they did not bring Israel back to good, while the removal of the ring did
